REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - FEBRUARY 25, 2021 - 07:00 P.M.
ZOOM VIDEO COMMUNICATIONS, MEETING ID # 832 2769 8352
LEGISLATIVE BODY MEMBERS MAY PARTICIPATE FROM THE CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER, 18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, OR VIA TELECONFERENCE AUTHORIZED BY STATE OF CALIFORNIA EXECUTIVE ORDERS N-25-20 AND N-29-20
* THE CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER REMAINS CLOSED TO THE PUBLIC *
INSTRUCTIONS FOR PUBLIC PARTICIPATION IN THIS MEETING ARE LISTED BELOW
*COVID-19 NOTICE*
To protect public health and safety during the local, state, and federally declared COVID-19 emergency, and in compliance with the current Los Angeles County Health Officer Order, the City Council Chamber remains closed to the public. As authorized by State of California Executive Orders N-25-20 and N-29-20 this meeting will be conducted via teleconference. Public observation and participation in this meeting will be facilitated through the methods described below.
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after the distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or by connecting to the ZOOM meeting described below.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting using any of the following methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Teleconference Participation: Live audio public comments can be made by connecting to the meeting using the information listed below. Public speakers will be queued to provide comment at the appropriate time during the meeting agenda and must be available at the time they are called upon to speak.
Cerritos Zoom meeting online link: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/83227698352
Cerritos Zoom Meeting call-in telephone number: (669) 900-6833
Cerritos Zoom Meeting ID: 832 2769 8352
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the teleconference meeting.

Items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by one motion. In addition, requests may be made of the staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. There will be no discussion or action taken on any of the items that may be presented during this agenda item.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD FEBRUARY
25, 2021, 7:00 P.M., IN HYBRID MODE FROM THE COUNCIL CHAMBER, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA AND VIA TELECONFERENCE AS AUTHORIZED BY
STATE OF CALIFORNIA EXECUTIVE ORDERS N-25-20 AND N-29-20, VIA ZOOM VIDEO
COMMUNICATIONS, MEETING ID# 832 2769 8352

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

  Mayor Solanki opened the meeting in honor of Los Angeles County Sheriff Deputy Thomas J.
  Albanese, who was killed in the line of duty today, and requested a moment of silence in his
  memory.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Naresh Solanki.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Bruce Barrows
  Council/Agency Member Grace Hu
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Chuong Vo
  Mayor/Chair Naresh Solanki

5.  Presentations/Appointments

  Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer, invited the public to participate in the two upcoming
  Charter Review meetings scheduled for March 1 and March 22, 2021, 2:00 p.m.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Mel Cortez requested a memorial in the Cerritos Sculpture Garden to honor Cerritos
  residents who had succumbed to the COVID-19 virus. He also requested the City explore
  options for a bike path and use the City’s Facebook Page to recruit Neighborhood Watch
  members. Last, he requested future Charter review study sessions to be conducted in
  the evening hours.

  Sylvester Ani requested the City Council explore options to place a cap on third-party
  delivery services in order to assist Cerritos restaurants.

  Noting there were no other individuals who provided written correspondence or elected
  to speak, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.
 City of Cerritos  February 25, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 2 of 7

7.  Consent Calendar

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of February 11,
  2021, 7:00 p.m. (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Hu, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of February 11, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of the Register of Demands

7B.1. Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated February 25, 2021
  (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Hu, to approve the Register of
  Demands as follows:

  City of Cerritos  02/25/2021  $ 8,670,524.65 (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

8A.  Review and consideration of the following actions and information related to the lease
  and improvement of a City-owned property located at 12616 183rd Street, Cerritos,
  California, 90703: (1) Adoption of a resolution of the City of Cerritos determining that
  the subject property is not required for other City purposes; (2) Authorization for the
  City of Cerritos (landlord) to lease the subject City-owned property to Eminent, Inc.,
  dba Revolve Clothing, for general office purposes; (3) Authorization for the City of
  Cerritos to execute and enter into a Parking and Access Easement Agreement with El
  Dorado Park Community Church, Inc., property owner of 18422 Bloomfield Avenue, to
  grant certain parking and access rights associated with the subject properties; and (4)
  Information related to building and site improvements under Public Referral Project
  2019-1 (COUNCIL).

  Items 8A and 8B were heard concurrently.

  Staff reports were given by Kristin Aguila, Advance Planning/Economic Development
  Manager, Dario Simoes, Assistant City Engineer, and Dennis Roy, Assistant City
  Attorney. A PowerPoint presentation was displayed.
 City of Cerritos  February 25, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 3 of 7

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8A.  (continued)

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and the public comments period.

  Jonathan Tam, representing Eminent, Inc., dba Revolve Clothing, the proposed tenant,
  thanked City Council and staff for their work on this matter and express the proposed
  tenant’s enthusiasm for this partnership with the City.

  Noting there were no other individuals who provided written correspondence or elected
  to speak, the Mayor declared the public hearing and the public comments period closed.

  MAIN MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to approve staff’s
  recommendation with the addition of two amendments, as listed in the final main
  motion. Further discussion ensued by the City Council.

  SUBSTITUTE MOTION (Motion died due lack of a second): It was moved by Hu to
  approve staff’s recommendation with the following two amendments to the 12616 183rd
  Street Lease (Single Tenant): 1. Increase the annual rent two percent (2%) per year,
  and 2. Restrict the tenant improvement period to a maximum of four (4) months. The
  motion died for lack of a second.

  MAIN MOTION (Approved): It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, as
  amended by the maker of the motion, to:

  1. Waive full reading of and adopt Resolution No. 2021-02, A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS DETERMINING THAT THE
  PROPERTY LOCATED AT 12616 183RD STREET IS NOT REQUIRED FOR OTHER
  CITY PURPOSES AND AUTHORIZING THE LEASE OF THE PROPERTY FOR
  COMMERCIAL DEVELOPMENT BUSINESS PURPOSES (COUNCIL); and

  2. Authorize the Mayor, or his designee, to execute, acknowledge, and consent to lease
  documentation for the subject property located at 12616 183 rd Street, Cerritos,
  California, 90703, in such form as prepared by the City Attorney and as the City
  Manager shall deem appropriate, including a lease agreement, and all related
  documents required or appropriate in connection with the completion of this lease
  transaction, pursuant to the following two (2) amendments highlighted in boldface
  italicized script:

  12616 183rd Street Lease (Single Tenant)

  Article 10 – Assignment and Sublease

  (a) Tenant shall not assign this Lease, sublet the Premises in whole or in part or
  otherwise transfer any interest in this Lease or to the Premises (collectively, a
  "Transfer") without Landlord's prior written consent, as approved at a City
  Council meeting, which shall not be unreasonably withheld; provided, that
  Tenant shall request such consent at least thirty (30) sixty (60) days prior to
  the proposed commencement date of the Transfer. The acceptance of rent from
  any other person shall not be deemed to be a waiver of any of the provisions of
  this Lease or to be a consent to any Transfer. Any Transfer consented to by
  Landlord shall not relieve Tenant (or its transferee) from obtaining Landlord's
  consent to any subsequent Transfer. Tenant shall provide Landlord with financial
  statements for the proposed transferee, a fully executed copy of the proposed
  assignment, LA/568981-17 19185-00384606.002 - 288716.12 S-15 32 sublease
  or other Transfer documentation and such other information as Landlord may
 City of Cerritos  February 25, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 4 of 7

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8A.  (continued)

  reasonably request. Notwithstanding anything above to the contrary, Tenant
  shall have the right to assign this Lease, or sublease a portion of the Premises, to
  an Affiliate without the consent of Landlord but upon written notice to Landlord;
  provided that any assignment or sublease shall not release Tenant of any of its
  obligations hereunder or waive or limit the application of those provisions in any
  way, and such assignment or sublease shall be pursuant to a form of assignment
  or sublease document acceptable to Landlord in its reasonable discretion. An
  "Affiliate" shall mean another person or entity that controls, is controlled by or
  under common control with the Tenant and which shares direct or indirect
  ownership with the Tenant.

  3. Authorize the Mayor, or his designee, to execute a Parking and Access Easement
  Agreement, in such form as prepared by the City Attorney and as the City Manager
  shall deem appropriate, providing various parking and access easements through
  and among one (1) parcel owned by the City of Cerritos located at 12616 183 rd
  Street, and two (2) privately-owned parcels located at 18422 Bloomfield Avenue
  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8B.  Review and consideration of an award of contract for the construction of site and
  building improvements at the City-owned property located at 12616 183rd Street,
  Project No. 18206, Bid No. 1419-21 (COUNCIL).

  Items 8A and 8B were heard concurrently.

  Staff reports were given by Kristin Aguila, Advance Planning/Economic Development
  Manager and Dario Simoes, Assistant City Engineer. A PowerPoint presentation was
  displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and the public comments period. Noting there
  were no individuals who provided written correspondence or elected to speak, the Mayor
  declared the public hearing and the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Barrows, to:

  1. Award a contract in the amount of $7,498,156.00 for the Construction of Site and
  Building Improvements at the City-owned property located at 12616 183rd Street,
  Project No. 18206, Bid No. 1419-21, to PCN3, Inc. and reject the other bids; and

  2. Authorize the City Manager, or his designee, to execute any project-related change
  orders (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  February 25, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 5 of 7

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of an informational update on the City's response to the
  COVID-19 local emergency (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Annie Hylton, City Librarian & Marketing Manager. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  provided written correspondence or elected to speak, the Mayor declared the public
  comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Hu, and seconded by Vo, to receive and file the
  informational report on the City's response to the COVID-19 local emergency
  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration of an award of contract for Professional Consulting Services to
  update the City’s Local Hazard Mitigation Plan, RFP No. 1420-21 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was presented by Ana Tenorio, Management Analyst.  A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  provided written correspondence or elected to speak, the Mayor declared the public
  comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Hu, and seconded by Vo, to:

  1.  Award a professional services contract in the amount of $23,892.00 to update the
  City’s Local Hazard Mitigation Plan, RFP No. 1420-21, to Risk Management
  Professionals, Inc. and reject the other proposals received; and

  2.  Authorize the appropriation and expenditure of funds in an amount not to exceed
  $23,892.00 for the update to the City’s Local Hazard Mitigation Plan; and

  3.  Authorize the City Manager, or his designee, to approve any change orders that
  may become necessary to complete the scope of work as described in the agenda
  report (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  February 25, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 6 of 7

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9C.  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS APPROVING AN ELECTRONIC AND COMPUTING
  DEVICE USE POLICY (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Aaron Benjamin, Information Technology Manager. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  provided written correspondence or elected to speak, the Mayor declared the public
  comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to waive full reading of and
  adopt Resolution No. 2021-03, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE
  CITY OF CERRITOS APPROVING AN ELECTRONIC AND COMPUTING DEVICE USE
  POLICY (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation.

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or
  Federal legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.

  None.

11.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings

  Reports were provided by Councilmember Barrows, Mayor Pro Tem Vo, and Mayor
  Solanki.

  CONSENSUS (Barrows): Directed the City Manager to prepare an instructional video to
  assist residents with utilizing the City’s OpenGov financial transparency website
  application.

  CONSENSUS (Vo): Directed the City Manager to implement a lighting memorial in the
  City’s Sculpture Garden to honor Cerritos residents who have succumbed to the COVID-
  19 virus and direct the Fine Arts and Historical Commission to review a long-term
  memorial concept once they resume regular meetings.

  CONSENSUS (Vo): Directed the City Manager to provide a report to the City Council
  regarding individual-type outdoor activities which can be offered by the City during the
  COVID-19 pandemic.

  Councilmember Vo offered the City’s condolences to the family, friends, and surrounding
  jurisdictions who had worked with Los Angeles County Sheriff Deputy Thomas J. Albanese,
  who had been killed in the line of duty. He requested the City’s flags be flown at half-staff
  through the day of memorial services for Deputy Albanese.
 City of Cerritos  February 25, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 7 of 7

12.  Closed Session

  None.

13.  Adjournment

  The meeting adjourned at 9:29 p.m.

  /s/Vida Barone
  Vida Barone, City Clerk/Agency Secretary
